claims.statement: dcode create_model applies its allowlist after provider inference but before credential bridging, provider profiles, and provider imports; blocked models therefore cannot cause those side effects.

The SDK exposes orthogonal beta profile registries: ProviderProfile controls string-model construction through init_chat_model, while HarnessProfile controls prompt, tools, middleware, and default-subagent behavior after model construction; both accept provider or provider:model keys and registration layers rather than replaces existing settings.

Provider-profile resolution merges an exact model profile over its provider profile, chains pre-initialization hooks and dynamic factories base first, and lets factory output override static profile kwargs while caller kwargs retain final precedence.

Harness-profile lookup selects an exact spec before provider fallback and merges model-level and provider-level fields; create_deep_agent resolves this profile for the main model and each declarative subagent before applying prompt, tool-description, and middleware changes.

dcode creates models only after policy validation, layers provider and per-model defaults with stored credentials and SDK provider profiles before runtime kwargs, and stamps the concrete model with the provider-specific retry budget used after runtime model switching.

dcode disables recognized provider SDK retry loops, stores the selected retry budget on each constructed model, and its model-node middleware uses that per-request budget so runtime model switches do not multiply retry attempts.

The effective dcode model-node retry budget is selected in descending precedence from --max-retries, provider-specific retry configuration, global retry configuration, and the built-in default; zero disables retries.
dcode 0.2.15 requires Python >=3.14,<3.15 and pins deepagents==0.7.42, while the deepagents 0.7.42 manifest supports Python >=3.11,<4.0; the SDK range does not widen dcode's released Python contract.
The deepagents 0.7.42 manifest requires LangChain >=1.5.2,<2.0.0, LangChain Core >=1.8.5,<2.0.0, langchain-anthropic >=1.7.13,<2.0.0, and langchain-google-genai >=4.4.3,<5.0.0.
A dcode provider class_path is a trusted configuration boundary because construction imports and instantiates the configured BaseChatModel class rather than using normal init_chat_model resolution.

dcode defers dotenv loading, project-context discovery, and credentials creation until the lazy credentials proxy is first used; bootstrap is lock-protected, runs once, and records failures while allowing the application to continue with the available environment.

For dcode dotenv loading, shell values take precedence over the nearest project dotenv, which takes precedence over the global profile dotenv; model construction can instead read an immutable context-local environment snapshot, and a present DEEPAGENTS_CODE_ variable shadows its canonical variable even when blank.

ModelConfig distinguishes no allowlist, deny-all, and exact-or-provider-wildcard admission policy; a malformed declared models.allowed fails closed as deny-all, and default-path loading preserves managed policy when the user configuration cannot be used.

dcode's picker uses separate persistence scopes for the main default, Auto classifier default, and summarization default, checks policy before saving, rejects a newly persisted model whose provider package is missing, and still permits clearing an unusable stored value.

Talon discovers selectable models from installed provider catalogs only when credentials are present in Talon's supplied environment, optionally augments the OpenAI catalog from a strictly validated LangSmith gateway endpoint, and requires exact catalog membership before building a nondefault model.

Talon caches each validated nondefault model under a lock and binds it in ACTIVE_MODEL only for the current invocation; unavailable or stale selections fall back to the startup default rather than failing the turn.

Talon's model-selection middleware overrides main-agent calls with the turn-scoped model without graph recompilation, while its replacement summarizer creates and caches selected-model-specific compaction middleware so context thresholds follow the selected model; subagents retain the startup summarizer.

Talon host-level model selections are operator-controlled and persisted across new conversations and restart; clearing to default removes persisted selection, and a switch made after a turn has started affects the next turn.

dcode's manifest is the canonical definition of user-tunable scalar configuration: it declares typed defaults, environment and TOML locations, CLI metadata, redaction, and merge behavior, while structured configuration remains in dedicated loaders.

The dcode resolver orders standard sources as managed policy, CLI, reload retention, environment, user config.toml, and manifest default; it returns typed values with provenance, tier health, masking, and diagnostics from one locked provider generation.

For scalar replacement options, invalid values fall through to lower-precedence sources and ultimately the typed default; the manifest owns bounded timeout and recursion options so invalid or out-of-range values cannot remove their finite safeguards.
The resolver preserves managed-policy safety during refresh by refusing unusable replacement providers and retaining the previously served usable snapshot when a managed refresh fails.

Accumulating structured configuration uses union or deep merge across valid tiers and records provenance; if a contributing value cannot safely be accumulated, resolution uses the strongest valid replacement rather than allowing a weaker source to override policy.

Talon's host persists a single global selected-model override only after an operator-requested model is validated and built; it captures that override when creating a turn, so later changes cannot alter an in-flight request.
Talon uses the same selected-model resolution path for context diagnostics as for invocation, so an unavailable selected model falls back to the startup model instead of preventing a context report.

Talon's `/effort` is an operator-controlled, model-specific override persisted separately from `/model`; it validates a requested label before writing, restores each model's saved setting when that model is selected again, and captures the effective setting into each new turn.

Talon translates only allowlisted model-specific effort labels to provider invocation settings, scopes those settings in ACTIVE_EFFORT for one invocation, merges nested extra_body thinking settings without overwriting unrelated settings, and does not apply the override in delegated subagents.
